_howTo: Radio talks with Walla Walla. Each lesson has two: "start" is typed out on the slip as the lesson opens, and "check" frames the lesson's check: its first line is typed above the check's questions and its last line under the score. In the start talk, each turn has Walla Walla saying "them" and the player picking one of up to three "replies" (none means a plain "Roger. Over."); a reply can have a "back" line, and every reply leads on to the next turn.

turns.them: Harrow, Walla Walla. Get out this morning’s map from the Bureau and look at the wind arrows. They run along the isobars, round the low, not into it. You’ve been using the rule about your back to the wind. This week, why it works.

replies.say: Why doesn’t the air just fill the low?
replies.back: That’s the question. The answer is under your feet, and it turns once a day.

turns.them: Short one this week. Questions at the end.
Harrow, Walla Walla. Questions. Read me the wind.
Now you know why it goes round. The coast next.
